page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is bundled as 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store, and the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves a strong multi-core CPU score of 81293.61 in stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 55910.68. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4502.68 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 215.93 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are a key strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 75.03 million operations per second and static web serving throughput peaking at 44.7 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1386.79 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.24xlarge offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage and 100 Gbps networking. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive and network-bound workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and high-throughput web serving. The primary tradeoff lies in single-threaded execution and LLM text generation, where the instance exhibits lower performance, making it less suitable for sequential processing tasks or heavy generative AI inference.
